meaning: the process of taking a legal dispute to court and fighting it out there rather than settling it between yourselves.
nuance: It emphasizes the formal court battle itself, not just any legal problem. A company avoids litigation by settling quietly; litigation means the case went public and expensive.

confusables.difference: Lawsuit is the legal action itself; litigation is the whole messy process and business of fighting it out.
A dispute is the disagreement; litigation is what happens when you drag it into court instead of resolving it yourself.

examples: The company faced lengthy litigation over the patent, costing them millions.
They wanted to avoid litigation, so they settled the contract dispute out of court.
memory_hook: Latin litigare — to quarrel; the -tion ending turns the verb into the noun for the whole drawn-out quarrel in court.
